ads.title: Take A · The declaration
ads.arc: The steroid era of advisor growth is ending. On a published schedule.
primary_text:
For twenty years, advisory growth came with enhancements. Rankings you could pay for. Scale you could borrow. Referrals you could rent from a custodian.

All three are being withdrawn at once. The New York Times just took apart the rankings. Rates took apart the roll-up math. And Schwab put an end date on rented referrals: January 5, 2027.

What is left is what a firm actually owns.

The benchmark shows where your firm actually stands: your metro, four named competitors, about 30 seconds to start. The report is yours either way.

Built for RIAs at and beyond $500M in AUM.

ads.title: Take B · The plaque
ads.arc: A ranking you could pay for was never a ranking.
primary_text:
The New York Times reported that Forbes fired its top editor over a secret $6 million payment from the founder of the research firm behind its advisor rankings. Morgan Stanley suspended participation days later.

Every firm bought the plaques because every firm bought the plaques. That was the era's rule, and nobody broke it. The era is what just ended.

Credibility is moving back to things that can be measured.

The benchmark shows where your firm actually stands: your metro, four named competitors, about 30 seconds to start. The report is yours either way.

ads.title: Take C · The ratchet
primary_text:
Schwab's minimum to refer a client out to an advisory firm held near $500,000 for two decades. In January 2026 it became $2 million. On January 5, 2027 it becomes $5 million, while Schwab hires thousands of financial consultants of its own.

No one did anything wrong. The channel's owner changed the terms, because it can. That is what renting a growth channel means, and the rent just went up for the last time.

The benchmark shows where your firm actually stands: your metro, four named competitors, about 30 seconds to start. The report is yours either way.

ads.title: Take D · The asterisk
primary_text:
When a firm eventually values a book, growth that arrived through someone else's brand gets discounted. Buyers pay multiples for the growth engine that transfers with the firm: the pipeline it owns, the visibility it earned, the clients who chose it directly.

The era that just ended inflated a lot of stat lines. The one starting rewards the real ones.

ads.title: Take E · The clean era
ads.arc: The future belongs to firms that earn their growth.
primary_text:
Own pipeline. Own clients. Own numbers.

The firms that thrive after an era ends are the ones whose results were theirs all along: visibility they earned, a site that converts, lead generation that runs on their own name. That has always been true in every field where the enhancements got taken away.
